fixes.explanation: David inquires of the LORD first, and the question is simple: "Should I go and attack these Philistines?" That's his move as soon as the report comes in. And the LORD tells him, "Go and attack the Philistines and save Keilah."

Afraid is the word, and they say it plainly: "Look, we are afraid here in Judah…" Then they ask, "how much more if we go to Keilah against the armies of the Philistines?" I honestly respect them for saying it out loud.
Restless isn't their word. Their word is "afraid." They tell David, "Look, we are afraid here in Judah…" and then they ask how much more afraid they'd be if they go to Keilah.

Comfortable isn't what the men say, friend. They tell David, "Look, we are afraid here in Judah…" Afraid and comfortable don't go together, and they want to know what happens if they march against the armies of the Philistines.
Weapons aren't mentioned at Keilah. The verse says David and his men "…carried off their livestock…" That's the only thing the text names them carrying off. I only give you what the verse gives me.

Saul's reasoning is that David "…has trapped himself by entering a town with gates and bars." To Saul, those gates and bars are what make it a trap. He even says God has delivered David into his hand.

Not quite, because the LORD says the opposite. David asks, "Will Saul come down, as Your servant has heard?" and the LORD answers, "He will." Then David and his men set out and depart from Keilah, and Saul declines to go forth (1 Samuel 23:13).
False is right, because the LORD says the opposite. David asks whether Saul will come down, and the answer is, "He will." Then David asks another question, this time about the citizens of Keilah.

The LORD actually says the opposite. David asks whether the citizens of Keilah will surrender him and his men into Saul's hand, and the answer is, "They will." Then David and his men set out and depart from Keilah (1 Samuel 23:13).
The text never says Saul punishes Keilah. What it says is that "…he declined to go forth." That's after Saul is told David has escaped from Keilah.

The verse says it directly: "Day after day Saul searched for him, but God would not deliver David into his hand." Saul keeps searching, and it still doesn't work. I think that's the part to remember when everything looks like it's closing in. God is the One keeping David out of Saul's hands.

It's Jonathan, Saul's son, who "…came to David in Horesh and strengthened his hand in God…" Saul has come out to take David's life, and his own son shows up to encourage him. I think David was glad to see him.

Jonathan says, "…you will be king over Israel…" Saul is still on the throne, and Jonathan is talking about what's coming. That's a big thing to say to a man Saul is hunting. I think it's the kind of encouragement a hunted man can use.
True. Jonathan says, "…you will be king over Israel, and I will be your second-in-command." Jonathan is Saul's son, and he names himself second to David. I think that's a rare kind of friend.

The text says the opposite. Jonathan tells David, "…you will be king over Israel, and I will be your second-in-command." Jonathan is Saul's son, and he says he'll be second to David. Second-in-command is right there in the verse.
True. Jonathan says, "Even my father Saul knows this is true." So Saul knows David will be king over Israel. Jonathan says it right after telling David not to be afraid.
They "…made a covenant before the LORD." A covenant is a formal agreement, and this one is made before the LORD. After that, David remains in Horesh while Jonathan goes home.
The text mentions no pillar. What David and Jonathan do is "…made a covenant before the LORD." It's an agreement between the two of them, made before the LORD. Then Jonathan goes home.
Fighting isn't the word they use. They tell Saul, "Is not David hiding among us in the strongholds at Horesh…" Hiding is their word, and they're the ones pointing out where.

Saul tells them, "Observe and find out all the places where he hides. Then come back to me with certainty…" He's been told David is extremely cunning, so he wants the full picture first. He asks them to scout, and he says, "…I will go with you."
The text says otherwise. When David is told about Saul's search, "…he went down to the rock and stayed in the Wilderness of Maon." He doesn't leave the Wilderness of Maon.
